new_statements.rule_in_words: Predictable word stress: primary stress on the penultimate syllable; if the final syllable contains a vowel cluster (diphthong, e.g. au, ai, ui, oi) stress shifts to that final syllable. In four-syllable words a weak (secondary) stress falls on the first syllable with primary stress on the penult. Reduplicated words keep the stress of each base. Stress is not written in the orthography (i.e. treated as non-contrastive).
new_statements.secondary_stress: Four-syllable words: weak stress on the first syllable, primary on the penult (e.g. [ˌgu.ma.'ma.wa]). Reduplications carry stress on each copy as in the base.
new_statements.exceptions: Final vowel cluster attracts stress to the ultima (tu.'kʷau, a.pu.'tui, au.'goi); a penult with a vowel cluster keeps penult stress ('bai.ɾɛn). Reduplicated forms retain base stress. No lexical exceptions listed.
new_statements.domain_note: Statements are about isolated words (citation forms) grouped by syllable count in an SIL Organised Phonology Data sheet; intonation treated separately (falling declarative, rising interrogative). Vowel length said to be non-phonemic. Draft posted 'as is' without peer review.
new_statements.identity_note: Source is the SIL-PNG Organised Phonology Data sheet for Maiwa of Milne Bay Province (villages Biniguni and Pumani), Dagan family, ISO mti = Glottolog maiw1251; no dialect distinction made. Not to be confused with Maiwa/Maiwala of other regions; the OPD explicitly identifies 'Trans New Guinea Phylum: Central Southeastern Stock, Dagan Family'.

sources.note: p.5-6 'Stress': in two- and three-syllable words stress falls on the penult, but on the ultima if the ultima contains a vowel cluster; in four-syllable words weak stress on the first syllable and primary stress on the penult; reduplicated forms keep the stress of the base; orthography: 'Stress is not marked.' Vowel length non-phonemic.
